commands: # Get instances from all three regions and check which are in public subnets # First, let's get instances from each region for region in us-east-1 us-west-1 us-west-2; do echo "=== Instances in $region ===" >&2 aws ec2 describe-instances --region "$region" --output json --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceId, State.Name, SubnetId, PrivateIpAddress, PublicIpAddress]' > /tmp/${region}_instances.json done # Now for each instance, we need to check if its subnet is public # A subnet is public if it has a route to an internet gateway check_if_public_subnet() { local region=$1 local subnet_id=$2 # Get the route table associated with this subnet route_table=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables --region "$region" --filters "Name=association.subnet-id,Values=$subnet_id" --output json --query 'RouteTables[0].RouteTableId' 2>/dev/null) if [ "$route_table" == "null" ] || [ -z "$route_table" ]; then # Try the main route table vpc_id=$(aws ec2 describe-subnets --region "$region" --subnet-ids "$subnet_id" --output json --query 'Subnets[0].VpcId' 2>/dev/null) route_table=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables --region "$region" --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$vpc_id" "Name=association.main,Values=true" --output json --query 'RouteTables[0].RouteTableId' 2>/dev/null) fi if [ "$route_table" != "null" ] && [ -n "$route_table" ]; then # Check if this route table has a route to an internet gateway (IGW) has_igw=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables --region "$region" --route-table-ids "$route_table" --output json --query "RouteTables[0].Routes[?GatewayId && starts_with(GatewayId, 'igw-')] | length(@)" 2>/dev/null) if [ "$has_igw" -gt 0 ]; then echo "public" return 0 fi fi echo "private" return 1 } # Process instances from each region for region in us-east-1 us-west-1 us-west-2; do instances=$(jq -r '.[][] | @json' /tmp/${region}_instances.json 2>/dev/null) while IFS= read -r instance_json; do [ -z "$instance_json" ] && continue instance_id=$(echo "$instance_json" | jq -r '.[0]') state=$(echo "$instance_json" | jq -r '.[1]') subnet_id=$(echo "$instance_json" | jq -r '.[2]') private_ip=$(echo "$instance_json" | jq -r '.[3]') public_ip=$(echo "$instance_json" | jq -r '.[4]') [ "$subnet_id" == "null" ] && continue is_public=$(check_if_public_subnet "$region" "$subnet_id") if [ "$is_public" == "public" ]; then echo "$region|$instance_id|$state|$subnet_id|$private_ip|$public_ip" fi done <<< "$instances" done

# Better approach: get all instances first, then check subnets declare -A public_subnets check_public_subnet() { local region=$1 local subnet_id=$2 cache_key="${region}:${subnet_id}" if [ -n "${public_subnets[$cache_key]}" ]; then echo "${public_subnets[$cache_key]}" return 0 fi # Get route tables for this subnet aws ec2 describe-route-tables \ --region "$region" \ --filters "Name=association.subnet-id,Values=$subnet_id" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.RouteTables[] | .RouteTableId' | while read -r rt_id; do # Check if any route goes to an IGW has_igw=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables \ --region "$region" \ --route-table-ids "$rt_id" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq '.RouteTables[0].Routes[] | select(.GatewayId and .GatewayId | startswith("igw-")) | .GatewayId' | wc -l) if [ "$has_igw" -gt 0 ]; then public_subnets[$cache_key]="public" echo "public" return 0 fi done # If no explicit association found, check main route table vpc_id=$(aws ec2 describe-subnets \ --region "$region" \ --subnet-ids "$subnet_id" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.Subnets[0].VpcId') if [ "$vpc_id" != "null" ] && [ -n "$vpc_id" ]; then main_rt=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables \ --region "$region" \ --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$vpc_id" "Name=association.main,Values=true" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.RouteTables[0].RouteTableId') if [ "$main_rt" != "null" ] && [ -n "$main_rt" ]; then has_igw=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables \ --region "$region" \ --route-table-ids "$main_rt" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq '.RouteTables[0].Routes[] | select(.GatewayId and .GatewayId | startswith("igw-")) | .GatewayId' | wc -l) if [ "$has_igw" -gt 0 ]; then public_subnets[$cache_key]="public" echo "public" return 0 fi fi fi public_subnets[$cache_key]="private" echo "private" } # Collect results results="" for region in us-east-1 us-west-1 us-west-2; do echo "Querying $region..." >&2 aws ec2 describe-instances \ --region "$region" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.Reservations[] | .Instances[] | "\(.InstanceId)|\(.State.Name)|\(.SubnetId)|\(.PrivateIpAddress)|\(.PublicIpAddress // "N/A")|\(.InstanceType)"' | while read -r line; do instance_id=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f1) state=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f2) subnet_id=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f3) private_ip=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f4) public_ip=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f5) instance_type=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f6) if [ -z "$subnet_id" ] || [ "$subnet_id" == "null" ]; then continue fi is_public=$(check_public_subnet "$region" "$subnet_id") if [ "$is_public" == "public" ]; then echo "$region|$instance_id|$state|$instance_type|$subnet_id|$private_ip|$public_ip" fi done done

# Simpler, more robust approach for region in us-east-1 us-west-1 us-west-2; do echo "Scanning $region..." >&2 aws ec2 describe-instances \ --region "$region" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.Reservations[] | .Instances[] | "\(.InstanceId)|\(.State.Name)|\(.SubnetId)|\(.PrivateIpAddress)|\(.PublicIpAddress // "N/A")|\(.InstanceType)"' | while read -r line; do [ -z "$line" ] && continue instance_id=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f1) state=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f2) subnet_id=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f3) private_ip=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f4) public_ip=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f5) instance_type=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'|' -f6) [ "$subnet_id" = "null" ] && continue # Check if this subnet is public by looking for IGW route has_igw=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables \ --region "$region" \ --filters "Name=association.subnet-id,Values=$subnet_id" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq '[.RouteTables[].Routes[] | select(.GatewayId != null) | select(.GatewayId | test("^igw-"))] | length') if [ "$has_igw" -eq 0 ]; then # Try main route table if no explicit association vpc_id=$(aws ec2 describe-subnets \ --region "$region" \ --subnet-ids "$subnet_id" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.Subnets[0].VpcId') if [ "$vpc_id" != "null" ] && [ -n "$vpc_id" ]; then has_igw=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables \ --region "$region" \ --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$vpc_id" "Name=association.main,Values=true" \ --output json 2>/dev/null | jq '[.RouteTables[].Routes[] | select(.GatewayId != null) | select(.GatewayId | test("^igw-"))] | length') fi fi if [ "$has_igw" -gt 0 ]; then echo "$region|$instance_id|$state|$instance_type|$subnet_id|$private_ip|$public_ip" fi done done
